questions.q: Nongkhnum, the river island described by the West Khasi Hills district portal, is formed by the divergence of which river near Diangsyiang and Diligim?
questions.e: The official district account says the Kynshi divides near Diangsyiang and Diligim into the northern Namliang and southern Phanliang streams. The land between the diverging channels forms Nongkhnum Island. The question tests the river system, not the names of the island's waterfalls.

questions.q: According to the West Khasi Hills district profile, Kyllang Rock near Mairang is composed of a single huge mass of which rock type?
questions.e: The district profile describes Kyllang Rock as a single, huge solid igneous rock at Mawnai, about 10 km from Mairang. Igneous rocks form through the cooling and solidification of magma or lava. The other options describe different rock origins or loose deposits.

questions.q: The official East Garo Hills profile attributes the formation of Ta'sek Lake near Songsak to the action of which river during the Great Earthquake of 1897?
questions.e: The Williamnagar profile states that Ta'sek Lake was formed by the River Damring during the Great Earthquake of 1897. The lake is near the Songsak block. This is a location-specific Meghalaya geography fact; it is not a question about the much larger Simsang river system.

questions.e: The official Williamnagar profile identifies Rong'bang Falls as a tributary of the Simsang River. The waterfall lies on the Tura–Williamnagar road beyond Rombagre village. A tributary is a smaller stream that flows into a larger river; the question checks the correct Garo Hills river association.

questions.q: Before Parliament may create or abolish a State Legislative Council under Article 169, what resolution must the State Legislative Assembly pass?
o: A simple majority of members present and voting only
A majority of the total membership and at least two-thirds of members present and voting
A unanimous resolution of the Assembly
A resolution supported by two-thirds of the total membership only
questions.e: Article 169 requires the Assembly resolution to satisfy two tests together: it must be supported by a majority of the total membership of the Assembly and by a majority of not less than two-thirds of members present and voting. After that, Parliament may provide for creation or abolition by law.

questions.q: Under Article 280, after the initial Commission, at what interval must the President ordinarily constitute a Finance Commission?
questions.e: Article 280 directs the President to constitute a Finance Commission at the expiration of every fifth year, or at such earlier time as the President considers necessary. The Commission recommends matters including the distribution of certain tax proceeds between the Union and the States.

questions.q: A Bill qualifies as a Money Bill under Article 110 only when it contains provisions dealing with which of the following?
o: Any matter of general public importance
Only matters listed in Article 110(1), such as taxation, borrowing or appropriation from the Consolidated Fund
Any Bill introduced in the Lok Sabha by a Minister
Any Bill that the Finance Minister describes as financial
questions.e: Article 110 defines a Money Bill by its subject matter. It must contain only provisions dealing with one or more of the specified matters, such as taxation, government borrowing, custody of the Consolidated Fund or appropriation from it. A Bill does not become a Money Bill merely because it concerns public finance generally.

questions.q: Which constitutional article requires the President to cause the estimated receipts and expenditure of the Government of India for a financial year to be laid before both Houses of Parliament?
questions.e: Article 112 calls this statement the Annual Financial Statement. It presents the estimated receipts and expenditure of the Government of India for the financial year. The Constitution separately provides for demands for grants and appropriation in the following articles.

questions.q: Who appoints the Comptroller and Auditor-General of India under Article 148?
o: The Prime Minister by executive order
The President by warrant under his hand and seal
The Speaker of the Lok Sabha
questions.e: Article 148 provides that the Comptroller and Auditor-General of India is appointed by the President by warrant under the President's hand and seal. The same article protects the CAG's independence by providing that removal is in like manner and on like grounds as a Supreme Court judge.

questions.q: For Parliament to legislate on a State List matter in the national interest under Article 249, what support must a Rajya Sabha resolution receive?
o: A majority of the total membership of Rajya Sabha
Not less than two-thirds of members present and voting
Three-fourths of the total membership of both Houses
A unanimous vote of the Rajya Sabha
questions.e: Article 249 requires a Council of States resolution supported by not less than two-thirds of the members present and voting. The resolution must declare that it is necessary or expedient in the national interest for Parliament to legislate on the specified State List matter. The power operates while the resolution remains in force.

questions.topic: Article 252 — State consent to Parliamentary law
questions.q: Two or more State Legislatures want Parliament to regulate a matter in the State List for them. Under Article 252, what is the necessary first step?
o: The Governors must jointly request Parliament
All Houses of the legislatures of those States must pass resolutions to that effect
The President must issue an ordinance
The Rajya Sabha must pass a two-thirds resolution under Article 249
questions.e: Article 252 allows Parliament to legislate for two or more States on a State List matter when resolutions to that effect are passed by all the Houses of the legislatures of those States. Another State may later adopt the law by passing its own resolution. This is distinct from Article 249's national-interest route.

questions.q: Article 256 permits the Union executive to issue directions to a State principally to ensure compliance with which laws?
o: Only laws made by the State Legislature
Laws made by Parliament and existing laws applicable in that State
Only laws passed by the Rajya Sabha
questions.e: Article 256 requires the executive power of every State to be exercised so as to ensure compliance with laws made by Parliament and existing laws applicable in that State. The Union's executive power extends to giving directions necessary for that purpose. It is a constitutional mechanism for ensuring legal compliance.

o: Recruitment and conditions of service of persons appointed to public services and posts

questions.q: Choose the meaning of the idiom 'at sixes and sevens' in the sentence: 'After the records were shifted, the files were left at sixes and sevens.'
o: In a state of confusion or disorder
questions.e: 'At sixes and sevens' means in a confused, disorganised or unsettled state. The sentence describes files that have been left without a proper arrangement. It does not mean that the files are literally numbered six and seven or divided into equal groups.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. Cambridge Dictionary — idiom 'at sixes and sevens'.

questions.q: In formal English, a 'disinterested observer' is best described as a person who is:
questions.e: 'Disinterested' traditionally means impartial or free from personal interest in the outcome. It should not be confused with 'uninterested', which means lacking curiosity or attention. In an official report, a disinterested observer is one who can assess the matter without personal bias.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. Cambridge Dictionary — 'disinterested'.

questions.q: The word 'abrogate' is closest in meaning to:
questions.e: 'Abrogate' means to formally end, repeal or abolish a law, agreement or established arrangement. It is stronger and more formal than simply delaying something. In administrative and legal writing, a rule may be abrogated by a competent authority through the appropriate legal process.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. Cambridge Dictionary — 'abrogate'.

questions.q: The office issued a digital acknowledgement in lieu of a paper receipt. The phrase 'in lieu of' means:
questions.e: 'In lieu of' means 'instead of' or 'in place of'. The sentence says that the digital acknowledgement was issued as a substitute for the paper receipt, not as an additional document. This phrase is common in formal administrative and legal writing.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. Cambridge Dictionary — 'in lieu of'.

questions.q: Choose the correct pronoun: 'The final decision rests between you and ___.'
questions.e: The preposition 'between' takes an object pronoun. Therefore 'me' is correct: 'between you and me'. 'I' is a subject pronoun, 'mine' is possessive, and 'myself' is a reflexive form that cannot replace the ordinary object pronoun here.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. Cambridge Dictionary — personal pronouns.

questions.q: Choose the correct completion: 'If I ___ in your position, I would verify the source before signing the note.'
questions.e: In a hypothetical or unreal condition, formal English commonly uses 'were' for all persons: 'If I were in your position'. The clause describes an imagined situation, not a factual past event. 'Was' is common in informal speech but 'were' is the standard subjunctive form in this construction.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. Cambridge Dictionary — hypothetical conditionals.

questions.q: A 'cogent argument' is one that is:
o: Persuasive because it is clear and well-reasoned
questions.e: 'Cogent' describes an argument or reason that is clear, logical and convincing. A cogent submission connects its evidence to its conclusion in a way that can be followed. It does not mean merely lengthy, emotional or frequently repeated.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. Cambridge Dictionary — 'cogent'.

questions.q: If an employee describes the day of receiving a long-awaited appointment order as a 'red-letter day', the phrase means:
o: A day marked by a legal notice
A particularly memorable or important day
A day when accounts are closed
questions.e: A 'red-letter day' is a day that is especially important, happy or memorable. The expression is often used for a significant personal or public event. In the sentence, receiving the appointment order makes the day memorable; it has nothing to do with the colour of a document.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. Cambridge Dictionary — 'red-letter day'.

questions.q: What compound interest is earned on ₹10,000 at 10% per annum for one year when interest is compounded half-yearly?
questions.e: Half-yearly compounding divides the annual rate into two periods. The rate per half-year is 10% ÷ 2 = 5%, and there are two periods. Amount = 10,000 × 1.05 × 1.05 = ₹11,025. Compound interest = 11,025 − 10,000 = ₹1,025.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. NCERT — Mathematics textbook resources.

questions.q: A vehicle travels the same distance at 40 km/h and 60 km/h. What is its average speed for the complete journey?
questions.e: For equal distances, average speed is not the simple arithmetic mean. Let each distance be d. Total distance is 2d and total time is d/40 + d/60 = d/24. Therefore average speed = 2d ÷ (d/24) = 48 km/h. The harmonic-mean formula gives the same result: 2ab/(a+b).
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. NCERT — Mathematics textbook resources.

questions.q: A can finish a job alone in 12 days and B in 18 days. They work on alternate days, beginning with A. How long will the job take?
questions.e: In two days, A and B together complete 1/12 + 1/18 = 5/36 of the job. Six two-day cycles complete 30/36 = 5/6 in 12 days. On day 13, A completes 3/36, leaving 3/36? After day 13 the completed work is 33/36; B completes 2/36 on day 14, leaving 1/36. A completes that fraction in (1/36) ÷ (1/12) = 1/3 day. Total time is 14⅓ days.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. NCERT — Mathematics textbook resources.

questions.q: A bag contains 5 red balls and 3 blue balls. Two balls are drawn one after another without replacement. What is the probability that both are red?
questions.e: The probability that the first ball is red is 5/8. After one red ball is removed, 4 red balls remain among 7 balls, so the probability that the second is red is 4/7. Multiply the conditional probabilities: (5/8) × (4/7) = 20/56 = 5/14.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. NCERT — Mathematics textbook resources.

questions.q: Two similar triangles have corresponding side lengths in the ratio 3:5. What is the ratio of their areas?
questions.e: For similar figures, areas vary as the square of the ratio of corresponding lengths. Squaring 3:5 gives 3²:5² = 9:25. The ratio 3:5 would apply to corresponding lengths, not areas; 27:125 would be a volume ratio for similar three-dimensional solids.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. NCERT — Mathematics textbook resources.

questions.q: A circle has radius 14 cm. What is the length of the minor arc subtended by a central angle of 90°? Use π = 22/7.
questions.e: A 90° sector is one quarter of a full circle. The full circumference is 2πr = 2 × 22/7 × 14 = 88 cm. One quarter of 88 cm is 22 cm. The formula is arc length = (θ/360°) × 2πr.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. NCERT — Mathematics textbook resources.

questions.q: A two-digit number has digits whose sum is 11. The tens digit is 3 greater than the units digit. What is the number?
questions.e: Let the units digit be u. The tens digit is u + 3. Since their sum is 11, u + (u + 3) = 11, so 2u = 8 and u = 4. The tens digit is 7, giving the number 74. Checking: 7 + 4 = 11 and 7 − 4 = 3.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. NCERT — Mathematics textbook resources.

questions.q: A train 180 metres long travels at 54 km/h. How long will it take to cross a platform 270 metres long?
questions.e: To clear the platform, the train's front must travel the train length plus the platform length: 180 + 270 = 450 metres. Convert 54 km/h to 15 m/s by multiplying by 5/18. Time = distance ÷ speed = 450/15 = 30 seconds.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. NCERT — Mathematics textbook resources.

questions.q: The variable y is inversely proportional to x. If y = 18 when x = 4, what is y when x = 6?
questions.e: For inverse variation, xy is constant. From the first pair, the constant is 4 × 18 = 72. When x = 6, y = 72/6 = 12. As x increases, y decreases in the same inverse proportion; multiplying x and y verifies the relationship.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. NCERT — Mathematics textbook resources.

questions.q: The present ages of A and B are in the ratio 4:5. After 6 years, their ages will be in the ratio 5:6. What is the sum of their present ages?
questions.e: Let the present ages be 4x and 5x. After six years, (4x+6)/(5x+6) = 5/6. Cross-multiplying gives 24x + 36 = 25x + 30, so x = 6. Their present ages are 24 and 30 years, and the sum is 54 years.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. NCERT — Mathematics textbook resources.

questions.q: The Permanent Settlement of Bengal, introduced in 1793, is most closely associated with which Governor-General?
questions.e: The Permanent Settlement was introduced under Lord Cornwallis in 1793. It fixed the land-revenue demand payable by zamindars to the East India Company, subject to the settlement's terms. It is distinct from later revenue arrangements that assessed cultivators or villages differently.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. NCERT — Our Pasts III, Ruling the Countryside.
questions.sourceName: NCERT — Our Pasts III, Ruling the Countryside

questions.q: Under the Mahalwari revenue arrangement, the unit with which the revenue settlement was made was generally the:
questions.e: The term 'mahal' referred to a village estate or revenue unit. Under the Mahalwari system, the revenue demand was assessed with reference to the village or mahal, with responsibility shared through its recognised proprietors. This differs from the Permanent Settlement's zamindari arrangement and the Ryotwari system's direct settlement with cultivators.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. NCERT — Our Pasts III, Ruling the Countryside.
questions.sourceName: NCERT — Our Pasts III, Ruling the Countryside

questions.q: Which feature best distinguishes the Ryotwari system from the Permanent Settlement?
o: Revenue was settled directly with individual cultivators or ryots
Revenue was permanently fixed with zamindars as a class
Revenue was collected only through village headmen in every region
questions.e: Under the Ryotwari system, the colonial state made the revenue settlement directly with individual cultivators, called ryots. The Permanent Settlement instead recognised zamindars as the intermediaries responsible for paying the fixed revenue demand. The systems differed in the recognised revenue-paying unit and the relationship between the state and cultivators.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. NCERT — Our Pasts III, Ruling the Countryside.
questions.sourceName: NCERT — Our Pasts III, Ruling the Countryside

questions.q: In the indigo-growing system described by NCERT, what did 'ryoti' cultivation mean?
o: Indigo grown on land owned and directly cultivated by the planter
Indigo grown by ryots on their own fields under contracts with planters
Indigo cultivated only on government-owned experimental farms
Indigo grown exclusively in forest clearings by tribal communities
questions.e: In ryoti cultivation, the planter contracted with peasants or ryots, often advancing money and requiring them to grow indigo on their own fields. It differed from nij cultivation, in which planters grew indigo on land under their direct control. The distinction helps explain the pressure placed on cultivators.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. NCERT — Our Pasts III, Ruling the Countryside.
questions.sourceName: NCERT — Our Pasts III, Ruling the Countryside

questions.q: Mahatma Gandhi's visit to Champaran in 1917 was connected primarily with the grievances of:
o: Mill workers demanding an eight-hour day
Soldiers protesting a new military uniform
questions.e: The Champaran movement arose from the plight of indigo cultivators in Bihar under the planters' system. NCERT records that Gandhi's visit in 1917 marked the beginning of the movement against the indigo planters. It is an early example of Gandhi's use of investigation, public mobilisation and non-violent resistance in India.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. NCERT — Our Pasts III, Ruling the Countryside.
questions.sourceName: NCERT — Our Pasts III, Ruling the Countryside

questions.q: The Santhal rebellion of 1855–56 is especially associated with the leadership of:
questions.e: The Santhal uprising of 1855–56 was led prominently by Sidhu and Kanhu, with other members of the Murmu family and supporters. It was directed against oppressive moneylenders, zamindars and colonial authority. The names should not be confused with Birsa Munda, whose movement arose later in the nineteenth century.

questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. NCERT — Our Pasts III, Tribals, Dikus and the Vision of a Golden Age.

questions.q: The Bardoli Satyagraha of 1928, led against an increase in land revenue, is closely associated with which leader?
questions.e: Vallabhbhai Patel led the Bardoli peasants' campaign in Gujarat against the enhanced land-revenue assessment. The movement's success strengthened his public leadership, and the title 'Sardar' became associated with him. The question concerns the leader, not the separate Champaran or Kheda campaigns.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. NCERT — Indian National Movement learning resources.

questions.q: At the Lahore session of the Indian National Congress in December 1929, the Congress adopted which objective?
o: Dominion status within the British Empire
Immediate acceptance of the Cabinet Mission Plan
questions.e: The Lahore session of December 1929, presided over by Jawaharlal Nehru, adopted Purna Swaraj as the Congress objective. The Congress called for 26 January 1930 to be observed as Independence Day. This marked a shift from the earlier demand for dominion status to the goal of complete independence.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. NCERT — Indian National Movement learning resources.
questions.sourceName: NCERT — Indian National Movement learning resources

questions.q: Because of Earth's rotation, a freely moving large-scale air current is deflected generally in which direction in the Northern Hemisphere?
o: To the left of its direction of motion
To the right of its direction of motion
questions.e: The Coriolis effect causes moving air and water to be deflected to the right in the Northern Hemisphere and to the left in the Southern Hemisphere. It arises from Earth's rotation and is zero at the equator in the idealised horizontal-motion description. It influences winds and ocean currents.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. NCERT — Fundamentals of Physical Geography.

questions.q: The Inter-Tropical Convergence Zone (ITCZ) is characterised mainly by the:
o: Convergence of the north-east and south-east trade winds near the equatorial low-pressure belt
Divergence of polar easterlies at the poles
Meeting of warm and cold ocean currents
Descent of dry air over subtropical high-pressure belts
questions.e: The ITCZ is a low-pressure belt near the thermal equator where the trade winds from the two hemispheres converge. Strong heating and rising moist air favour cloud formation and rainfall. Its seasonal north–south migration is an important part of the monsoon system.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. NCERT — Fundamentals of Physical Geography.

questions.q: On a weather map, an isohyet joins places that receive equal:
questions.e: An isohyet is a line joining locations with equal rainfall over a specified period. By contrast, isobars join equal atmospheric pressure and isotherms join equal temperature. Isohyets help geographers and planners map the spatial distribution of precipitation.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. NCERT — Fundamentals of Physical Geography.

questions.q: In a soil profile, the O horizon is primarily associated with:
o: Accumulation of clay washed down from upper layers
A layer of permanently frozen groundwater
questions.e: The O horizon is the surface organic layer containing leaf litter and decomposing organic matter. Below it, the A horizon is commonly mineral topsoil mixed with humus, while the B horizon often receives materials leached from upper layers. Recognising the horizons helps interpret soil development.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. NCERT — Fundamentals of Physical Geography.

questions.q: A Mercator map is useful for navigation because it preserves local angles and directions, but what important distortion increases towards the poles?
o: The equator is shown as a point
Distances along every route become exact
questions.e: The Mercator projection is conformal: it preserves local angles and makes constant-bearing routes appear as straight lines. However, its scale increases with latitude, greatly enlarging areas near the poles. Greenland therefore appears much larger relative to equatorial regions than its true area warrants.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. NCERT — Fundamentals of Physical Geography.

questions.q: The term 'doldrums' traditionally refers to the:
o: Subtropical belt of descending dry air
Equatorial low-pressure belt with weak and variable surface winds
questions.e: The doldrums are associated with the equatorial low-pressure belt, where intense heating causes air to rise and surface winds may be weak or variable. The region is also associated with the Inter-Tropical Convergence Zone. It is different from the subtropical high-pressure belts, often called horse latitudes.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. NCERT — Fundamentals of Physical Geography.

questions.q: Other factors being comparable, why do inland locations often experience a larger annual temperature range than coastal locations?
o: Land heats and cools more rapidly than the sea
Land has a higher specific heat capacity than water
Ocean currents stop all seasonal temperature change
Coastal air contains no water vapour
questions.e: Land generally heats and cools more rapidly than water. The sea moderates nearby temperatures because water has a higher specific heat capacity and ocean mixing distributes heat. Far inland, this maritime influence weakens, so summers may be hotter and winters colder, producing a larger annual temperature range.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. NCERT — Fundamentals of Physical Geography.

questions.q: A fjord is best described as:
o: A deep, narrow glacial valley flooded by seawater
A river island formed by deposition
A limestone cave with underground streams
questions.e: A fjord is a deep, narrow inlet formed when a glacially carved valley is flooded by the sea. Its steep sides reflect the erosional work of a glacier. Fjords are common along formerly glaciated high-latitude coasts, especially in Norway and parts of New Zealand and Chile.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. NCERT — Fundamentals of Physical Geography.

questions.q: At the level of a producing unit, Gross Value Added (GVA) is calculated as:
o: Value of output minus intermediate consumption
Value of output plus intermediate consumption
Gross fixed capital formation minus depreciation
questions.e: GVA measures the value created by a producer. It is calculated as the value of output minus the value of intermediate goods and services consumed in production. This prevents the same intermediate input from being counted again at each stage of the production chain.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. NCERT — Statistics for Economics.

questions.q: A government has a fiscal deficit of ₹8 lakh crore and pays ₹3 lakh crore as interest on past debt. What is its primary deficit?
questions.e: Primary deficit equals fiscal deficit minus interest payments. Therefore ₹8 lakh crore − ₹3 lakh crore = ₹5 lakh crore. The measure shows the current borrowing requirement after excluding interest payments arising from accumulated past debt.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. Union Budget — Budget at a Glance and fiscal indicators.
questions.sourceName: Union Budget — Budget at a Glance and fiscal indicators

questions.q: Which government expenditure is most clearly classified as capital expenditure?
o: Payment of monthly salaries to staff
Construction of a new public bridge
questions.e: Capital expenditure generally creates assets or reduces liabilities. Building a public bridge creates a durable public asset, so it is capital expenditure. Salaries, stationery and electricity bills are ordinarily revenue expenditure because they meet recurring operating costs rather than directly creating a new asset.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. Union Budget — Budget at a Glance and expenditure classification.
questions.sourceName: Union Budget — Budget at a Glance and expenditure classification

questions.q: Proceeds received by the Union Government from selling part of its equity holding in a public sector enterprise are ordinarily classified as:
questions.e: Disinvestment proceeds are classified as non-debt capital receipts. They provide funds through the sale of government assets or equity holdings and do not create a repayment obligation in the way borrowings do. They are therefore distinct from both tax revenue and debt-creating receipts.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. Union Budget — Receipts Budget.

questions.q: In a simplified economy, a sharp increase in government borrowing may raise interest rates and reduce private investment. This effect is known as:
questions.e: The crowding-out effect describes how increased government borrowing may put upward pressure on interest rates or absorb available loanable funds, leaving less finance for private investment. The strength of the effect depends on economic conditions, monetary policy and the availability of savings; it is not inevitable in every situation.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. NCERT — Introductory Macroeconomics and public finance concepts.

questions.q: Which example best illustrates an automatic stabiliser in a modern tax-and-transfer system?
o: Parliament votes on a new road project every month
Income-tax collections fall automatically when taxable incomes decline during a downturn
The central bank announces a new policy rate after every election
A government sells a public enterprise to finance a festival
questions.e: An automatic stabiliser changes government revenue or expenditure without a new discretionary policy decision. When incomes fall, progressive income-tax collections usually decline automatically, cushioning disposable income. Some transfer payments may also rise as eligibility increases. This helps moderate economic fluctuations.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. NCERT — Introductory Macroeconomics and public finance concepts.
questions.sourceName: NCERT — Introductory Macroeconomics and public finance concepts

questions.q: If an export price index is 120 and an import price index is 100, what is the terms-of-trade index using export prices divided by import prices and multiplied by 100?
questions.e: The terms-of-trade index is (export price index ÷ import price index) × 100. Substituting the values gives (120 ÷ 100) × 100 = 120. A rise in this index means export prices have increased relative to import prices, other things being equal.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. NCERT — Introductory Macroeconomics and international trade concepts.
questions.sourceName: NCERT — Introductory Macroeconomics and international trade concepts

questions.q: In a simple Keynesian model, if the marginal propensity to consume is 0.8 and there are no taxes or imports, what is the simple expenditure multiplier?
questions.e: The simple multiplier is 1/(1−MPC). With MPC = 0.8, the multiplier is 1/0.2 = 5. An initial increase in autonomous expenditure can therefore produce a larger total change in equilibrium income as the spending circulates through successive rounds. The result assumes the simplified model stated in the question.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. NCERT — Introductory Macroeconomics.

questions.q: Which of the following is ordinarily revenue expenditure rather than capital expenditure for a government department?
o: Construction of a new hospital building
Routine annual maintenance of office equipment
Acquisition of land for a public project
questions.e: Routine annual maintenance of office equipment is generally revenue expenditure because it meets recurring operating costs and does not normally create a new asset. Construction of a hospital, a bridge or acquisition of land for a public project is ordinarily treated as capital expenditure under government budget classification.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. Union Budget — Budget at a Glance and expenditure classification.

questions.q: Which cells are the principal source of insulin in the human pancreas?
o: Alpha cells of the islets of Langerhans
Beta cells of the islets of Langerhans
Delta cells of the islets of Langerhans
questions.e: Insulin is secreted by the beta cells of the pancreatic islets of Langerhans. It helps lower blood glucose by promoting glucose uptake and storage in responsive tissues. Alpha cells mainly secrete glucagon, which raises blood glucose. The distinction is important in understanding endocrine regulation of metabolism.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. NCERT — Science and Biology textbooks.

questions.q: In the human respiratory system, the exchange of oxygen and carbon dioxide between air and blood occurs mainly across the walls of the:
questions.e: Alveoli are tiny air sacs surrounded by dense networks of capillaries. Their thin, moist walls and large combined surface area allow oxygen to diffuse into the blood and carbon dioxide to diffuse from the blood into the alveolar air. The trachea and bronchi mainly conduct air.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. NCERT — Science and Biology textbooks.

questions.q: The oxygen-carrying capacity of red blood cells depends mainly on haemoglobin, whose oxygen-binding component contains which element?
questions.e: Haemoglobin contains heme groups with iron at their centre. Oxygen binds reversibly to the iron-containing heme, allowing red blood cells to transport oxygen from the lungs to body tissues. Iron deficiency can reduce haemoglobin production and contribute to anaemia.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. NCERT — Science and Biology textbooks.

questions.q: In terms of electron transfer, oxidation is defined as:
o: Loss of protons from the nucleus
questions.e: Oxidation is loss of electrons, while reduction is gain of electrons. The two processes occur together in a redox reaction because electrons lost by one species are gained by another. The mnemonic OIL RIG—Oxidation Is Loss, Reduction Is Gain—helps remember the definitions.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. NCERT — Science and Chemistry textbooks.

questions.q: At the same temperature, a solution of pH 3 has how many times the hydrogen-ion concentration of a solution of pH 5?
questions.e: The pH scale is logarithmic: a decrease of one pH unit represents a tenfold increase in hydrogen-ion concentration. A difference of two units therefore represents 10 × 10 = 100 times. Thus the pH 3 solution has 100 times the hydrogen-ion concentration of the pH 5 solution.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. NCERT — Science and Chemistry textbooks.

questions.q: When pure ice at its melting point changes into liquid water at the same temperature, the heat absorbed is called:
questions.e: Latent heat of fusion is the heat required to change a unit mass of a substance from solid to liquid at its melting point without a change in temperature. The supplied energy changes the state by overcoming intermolecular forces rather than raising the temperature.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. NCERT — Science and Physics textbooks.

questions.q: When a swimmer pushes water backward and moves forward, which law best explains the forward motion?
o: Law of conservation of electric charge
questions.e: Newton's third law states that for every action there is an equal and opposite reaction. The swimmer pushes water backward; the water exerts an equal and opposite force on the swimmer, pushing the swimmer forward. The action and reaction forces act on different bodies, so they do not cancel each other on one body.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. NCERT — Science and Physics textbooks.

questions.q: A force of 100 newtons acts normally on an area of 0.5 square metre. What pressure is produced?
questions.e: Pressure is force divided by the area over which it acts: P = F/A. Here P = 100 ÷ 0.5 = 200 pascals. For the same force, reducing the contact area increases pressure; this explains why a sharp blade cuts more easily than a blunt one.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. NCERT — Science and Physics textbooks.

questions.q: In a chemical reaction carried out in a sealed container, which statement expresses the law of conservation of mass?
o: The mass of products is always greater than reactants
The total mass of reactants equals the total mass of products
Mass disappears when a gas is formed
Only the mass of solid substances is conserved
questions.e: The law of conservation of mass states that matter is neither created nor destroyed in a chemical reaction. In a closed system, the total mass before reaction equals the total mass after reaction. If a gas escapes from an open vessel, the measured mass may appear to decrease, but the total matter is still conserved.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. NCERT — Science and Chemistry textbooks.

questions.q: In the modern periodic table, a vertical column is called a:
questions.e: A vertical column in the modern periodic table is a group, while a horizontal row is a period. Elements in the same group often show similar chemical properties because of related valence-electron configurations. The terms should not be interchanged when reading periodic trends.
